OnPlay.maps_to: DramaticEntranceCard.on_play, routed per-enemy by the framework (colorless_attacks.py:73-77; combat.py:481-487)
OnPlay.issue: The damage, the target set and the single hit are all faithful: `DamageCmd.Attack(11).FromCard(this).TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)` (DramaticEntrance.cs:40-42) hits every living opponent once, and the sim's framework routing calls `on_play` once per living enemy because `handles_own_routing` is left False, filtering on `is_gone` (combat.py:483-484), which is the right analogue of AttackCommand's `where c.IsAlive`. ALL-ENEMIES FAN-OUT: C# passes the whole valid-target list to ONE `CreatureCmd.Damage(targets: validTargets)` call (AttackCommand.cs:650), which computes every target's DamageResult first, runs the after-damage hooks over all of them, and only then calls `await Kill(killedCreatures)` for the whole batch (CreatureCmd.cs:372-409). The sim issues a SEPARATE `DamageCmd.deal` per enemy, so each enemy's death -- and any on-death effect -- fully resolves before the next enemy is damaged. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/conflagration's OnPlay entry (rule 3). DORMANT: no ported Ironclad-reachable monster has an on-death effect that changes a sibling's incoming damage or block, so the batched and sequential orders reach the same end state. Live the moment such a monster is ported. Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (38), the fullscreen VFX (39) and ExtraRunAssetPaths (16).
